steps.label: Plant tissues
lines: Meiosis takes place in the diploid sporogenous

lines.text: Megasporogenous tissue of the ovule — gives

steps.why: Meiosis is the division that halves the chromosome number, so it can only happen in the tissue that makes spores or gametes. In a flowering plant those two tissues sit inside the anther and inside the ovule.
common_mistakes: Writing 'anther' and 'ovule' alone. Name the tissue, not the organ.
Naming root tips or shoot tips. Those grow by mitosis.
steps.memory_tip: Micro from the anther, mega from the ovule: small spores from the male part, large spore from the female part.
steps.margin_note: Two plant tissues by name, one line each.

steps.label: Animal tissue

lines.text: Animals — germinal epithelium of the gonads (testis and ovary).

lines: These diploid mother cells divide by meiosis and
steps.why: Animals have no spore stage, so meiosis happens directly in the tissue that lines the gonad and makes the gametes.
common_mistakes: Writing 'testis and ovary' without naming the germinal epithelium.
steps.memory_tip: Plants make spores, animals make gametes, but both do it by meiosis.
steps.margin_note: One line for animals. Both marks are for naming tissues.

insider_note: Three tissue names carry this answer: microsporogenous, megasporogenous, germinal epithelium.
